subject: ACME - private deployment connectivity checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Nov 2025 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME - private deployment connectivity checklist & next steps

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the Private VPC path (vs hosted API / Dedicated):

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- You want production-grade inference inside your AWS account using PrivateLink (preferred) or VPC peering as fallback.
- Requirements: no egress to public internet for inference traffic, allowlist-based access for control plane, and predictable throughput for peak trading windows.
- Compliance: SOC2 + network audit evidence will be needed for procurement.

Immediate asks from Redwood to unblock qualification:
1) Can you confirm whether your infra team prefers PrivateLink or peering? (we heard PrivateLink but want explicit)
2) Send a point-of-contact for networking (primary + backup) and an initial egress/ingress IP range if you have one.
3) Fill the attached allowlist template with the team’s NAT/egress IPs — we’ll validate routing and map to our PrivateLink endpoints.

I attached an allowlist template and a short PrivateLink reference doc. If PrivateLink works, our onboarding takes ~3 weeks for configuration + validation; peering adds additional security review and typically takes longer.

Next steps I propose:
- Bob (ACME): populate the allowlist template and reply in 48 hours
- ACME network POC joins a short tech kickoff (30 min) with Aditya and Rachel to exchange VPC IDs and account numbers
- I’ll open a HubSpot deal record and attach procurement checklist items so procurement has visibility

We’re available tomorrow 10–12 PST for the tech sync if that helps.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Attachments: acme_allowlist_template.csv, redwood_privatelink-reference.pdf

Date: Wed, 26 Nov 2025 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME - private deployment connectivity checklist & next steps

Thanks Alice — 11:00 PST tomorrow works for us. Quick technical clarifications before the sync so we can prepare: 

- For PrivateLink we’ll need your AWS account number(s) and the specific VPC IDs where the interface endpoints will be created. If you prefer we can also support a VPC peering flow but it requires additional routing and security review.
- For the allowlist: the format in our template expects public egress NAT IPs (not private 10/172/192 ranges). If you’re behind NAT, please include the public IPs that your VPC uses to reach the internet.
- Throughput note: please add expected RPS and average prompt length (tokens) for peak windows — we’ll use that to size Dedicated vs shared capacity in the proposal if you want guaranteed throughput.

I’ll bring our PrivateLink runbook to the sync and a checklist to validate IAM/route table requirements.

See you tomorrow,
Aditya
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Bob Chen <bob.chen@acmeai.com>

Date: Wed, 26 Nov 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME - private deployment connectivity checklist & next steps

Aditya / Kimberly —

Appreciate the notes. A few clarifications from infra after a quick run-through: 
1) We can provide AWS account numbers and VPC IDs during the tech sync; prefer to share those in the meeting rather than email for initial exchange (we’ll paste them in the meeting chat).
2) Attached is a cleaned allowlist (acme_allowlist_template.csv) with public NAT IPs — please confirm these map to the PrivateLink endpoints you’ll provision.
3) Peak sizing: during market open (09:30–10:00 ET) we expect ~150 RPS with average 120 tokens per prompt; sustained 60 RPS off-peak. If Dedicated capacity is required we’re open to a committed plan — curious about ballpark pricing for a 3-node pool.

Also — procurement wants an evidence list for SOC2/network controls. Can Redwood supply a short network controls checklist and a copy of your SOC2 scope statement? We’ll add that to the internal ticket.

Thanks,
Bob Chen
Network Operations
ACME AI

Perfect, thanks for the cleaned allowlist and the sizing numbers — that’s extremely helpful. Action items we’ll take on from Redwood: 
- Aditya & Rachel: provision the PrivateLink runbook and validate the IPs in the attached CSV against our endpoint assignment (we’ll return a mapping table and recommended route table entries).
- I will draft a short SOC2/network evidence checklist and link to our SOC2 scope doc (non-confidential summary) — attaching redwood_privatelink-reference.pdf now.
- Pricing/ops: I’ll engage our sales lead to provide a 3-node Dedicated ballpark and a hosted failover cost comparison; expected ETA EOD Friday.

Proposed next meeting: tech validation + endpoint exchange (30 min) on Fri 11/28 at 11:00 PST — is that OK for you? If so we’ll send a calendar invite and a pre-meeting checklist.

Thanks again — we’ll treat this as a high-priority onboarding path and will share the endpoint mapping once Aditya validates.

Best,
